rulings.restated: Input — Gross receipts or sales of this business for 2025, including all amounts reported to you on Forms 1099-NEC, 1099-MISC and 1099-K for this business (zero if none)
rulings.model: The IRS asks only for gross receipts and 'amounts properly shown on your Forms 1099-NEC', telling filers to check Forms 1099 'for business income that must be reported on this line'. Line 6 separately takes 'Prizes and awards related to your trade or business' and similar items that can appear on Form 1099-MISC, so 'all amounts reported ... on Forms 1099-MISC' can put line 6 income on line 1.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: model right; fixed (BUG-0067). The question asked for all amounts on Forms 1099-MISC, which can include line 6 income such as prizes and awards (i1040sc p. 6, Line 6). It now asks for amounts properly shown on Forms 1099-NEC and other gross receipts reported on a Form 1099, not the other business income asked separately. Not re-reviewed on the new wording.

rulings.restated: Add helper "50% of the meals subject to the 50% limit" and helper "80% of the meals under the hours of service limits".
rulings.model: Only the 50% and 80% categories are provided. The instructions also say 'you can fully deduct meals and incidentals furnished or reimbursed to an employee if you properly treat the expense as wages', and likewise for amounts reported on Form 1099-NEC. These 100% meals have no place, and no refusal names them.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope gap recorded; restatement accepted for the meals it asks. Meals fully deductible (treated as wages, or reported on Form 1099-NEC; i1040sc p. 10) have no input; a filer who entered them at 50% would understate the deduction. Left for the owner as TASKS.md T-042 (a 100% input or a refusal).

rulings.restated: Add helper "50% of the meals subject to the 50% limit", helper "80% of the meals under the hours of service limits", and helper "Meals and incidentals not subject to the 50% limit, deducted in full".
rulings.model: The 50% and 80% rates and the two full-deduction cases (wages subject to withholding; nonemployee amounts reported on Form 1099-NEC) match the text. The other fully deductible categories in the helper (client reimbursements, employee recreation, food for the public, meals sold) are not in the given text, which only refers to 'chapter 5 of Pub. 15 ... for details and other exceptions'.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: owner ruling (T-042; amb.2025.meals_full_exceptions); restatement accepted. The 50% and 80% rates and the two full-deduction cases match i1040sc p. 10 as the model says. The other categories come from Pub. 463 (2025) p. 16, Exception to the 50% Limit for Meals, which the instruction reaches through 'See chapter 5 of Pub. 15 ... for details and other exceptions. See also chapter 8 of Pub. 334': Pub. 15 chapter 5 lists no exceptions and Pub. 334 refers to Pub. 463. The model was given the i1040sc pages only, so it could not see that list.

rulings.restated: Input — Did you "materially participate" in the operation of this business during 2025 (for example, you worked in it more than 500 hours, or your work was substantially all the work done in it, or more than 100 hours and at least as much as anyone else; see the seven tests in the instructions for line G), and is the business something other than a rental activity?
rulings.model: The restatement leaves out the oil and gas exception. The IRS text says to check Yes if 'you meet any of the material participation tests ... or the exception for oil and gas applies', and a working interest 'is not a passive activity'. Such a filer would answer No and be refused as passive, which the refusal does not name.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: fixed (BUG-0064). The question now includes the exception for oil and gas (i1040sc p. 4, line G; p. 5, Exception for oil and gas), so a working interest is answered Yes and not refused as passive.
